question: Can we hold and read from a mushaf while praying taraweeh?
answer:
It is a standard question, and it is something that doesn't require rethinking through. Realize we're talking about the nafil salahs, not the fard. The taraweeh prayer is a nafil, or sunnah; it is not fard, because obligatory is something else. The answer to this question is actually very clear to the majority of scholars.

In Sahih al-Bukhari we have a hadith, or an athar, of Aisha radiyallahu 'anha, that Aisha would command her freed slave Dhakwan to lead them in salah, and Dhakwan, because he was not a hafidh, would recite from the mushaf. And this is in Sahih Bukhari: *wa kana yaqra'u min al-mushaf*, he would recite from the mushaf. And this is very explicit, very clear; you cannot get more explicit. And it is in Sahih Bukhari, even though it's in mu'allaq form, but it is a hasan hadith. And that is that Aisha radiyallahu 'anha commanded her mawla Dhakwan, during the nights of Ramadan, to lead them in salah. This is after the death of the Prophet. Aisha would not go to pray in the masjid; she would pray in her house, and she had a freed slave, a servant, who would lead them in salah, but he had not memorized the Qur'an, so he would lead from the mushaf. And this is something very explicit.

The famous scholar Ibn Shihab al-Zuhri (and al-Zuhri died 129 Hijrah, and he is one of the greatest, if not the greatest, scholars of the Tabi'in; the Tabi' al-Tabi'in is really his main generation; one of the greatest 'ulama of Islam, al-Zuhri), al-Zuhri was asked about a man who recites from the mushaf during Ramadan. And al-Zuhri, who met some of the students and the sons of the Sahabah, al-Zuhri met some of the main sons of the Sahabah, al-Zuhri said, "The best amongst us, I remember them, they would read from the mushaf." This is al-Zuhri saying this. So it was a well-known, well-accepted habit that during the nights of Ramadan, when people would lead them in salah, they would hold the mushaf.

And in the *Mudawwanah* of Sahnun, which is one of the earliest books of Maliki fiqh, and the one who wrote it is a student of Imam Malik, he said that I asked Imam Malik about this issue. So Imam Malik, and again he is a person who is living in Medina two generations after the Prophet ﷺ, Imam Malik said there is no harm in carrying the mushaf for the imam in Ramadan for the nafl prayer, meaning for the tahajjud, because tahajjud is nafl, ya'ni qiyam. Meaning a nafil here is that it is not the fard prayer, so not for Isha. There is no harm for the imam to carry the mushaf in the nights of taraweeh. Basically, this is Imam Malik explicitly saying it, and that's the standard Maliki madhhab.

And Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal was asked about this, and he said, "*La ba'sa an yusalliya bil-nas al-qiyam wa huwa yanzuru fil-mushaf*." There is no harm, there's no problem at all, it's not even makruh, nothing: no problem for the imam to carry the mushaf, and he is leading the people in salah and he is looking at the mushaf. Again, this is for the taraweeh prayer; again, we're not talking about the fard prayer.

And Imam al-Nawawi in his *Majmu'*: so we talked about the Maliki madhhab, Imam Malik is explicit; we talked about the Hanbali madhhab, Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal is explicit; and the greatest scholar of the Shafi'i madhhab in the medieval times is Imam al-Nawawi. Imam al-Nawawi in his *Majmu'* says that if he leads from the Qur'an, from the mushaf, and he recites the Qur'an from the mushaf, regardless of whether he is a hafidh or not, it does not matter, and the salah is valid and correct. So he said that the salah is going to be valid if the person leads from the mushaf; there is no problem here.

So this is the Shafi'i school, the Maliki school and the Hanbali school, three of them. And I also quoted to you Aisha, our mother, way before any of these imams. And I quoted to you Ibn Shihab al-Zuhri, who was a well-travelled scholar. He had lived in Medina, he lived in Damascus, he met the sons of the Sahabah, and he said, "We all used to do this. The greatest people I met, they would do this." So it is something that the majority of the ummah has accepted.

Obviously, I have left one school, and that is the school that is the strictest in this regard. And we respect all of the schools, no problem with that, but you should be aware that these schools exist and they have their differences. And of course, the school that is left is the one school that is the strictest in this regard, and that is the Hanafi school. And the Hanafi school, generally speaking, was reluctant to open this door.

Imam al-Kasani, in his famous book *Bada'i' al-Sana'i'*... and by the way, I have to say this, just a bit, about *Bada'i' al-Sana'i'*. Imam al-Kasani died 587, I want to say, 587 Hijrah. And Imam al-Kasani was a great student of Imam al-Samarqandi, and Imam al-Samarqandi had written a book of Hanafi fiqh, and Imam al-Kasani was his student. And so Imam al-Kasani wrote what is considered to be one of the greatest classics of the Hanafi school, called *Bada'i' al-Sana'i'*, and he presented it to his teacher as a commentary on the book that his teacher al-Samarqandi had written. And this teacher was so impressed with the book (subhanAllah, this became a joke for later Hanafis, and it's a true story), he said, "This book, I will consider it to be the mahr for my daughter's hand in marriage." And he gave his daughter in marriage to his main student, and he said the mahr of the marriage is going to be this book, subhanAllah. So the book *Bada'i' al-Sana'i'* became the mahr for the marriage of Imam al-Kasani, subhanAllah. Those were different types of mahr. I don't know if any of our current sisters would accept a mahr to be a written multi-volume book of Hanafi fiqh. Allahu al-musta'an. Anyway, jokes aside, what was I saying?

*Bada'i' al-Sana'i'* of al-Kasani. Yes. So Imam al-Kasani writes in his *Bada'i' al-Sana'i'*, he mentions from Abu Hanifa (and the reason I say this is I could not find it in *al-Mabsut*, which is an earlier book), but Imam al-Kasani writes that Abu Hanifa rahimahullahu ta'ala considered the salah to be batil, null and void, if somebody held the mushaf. Okay, so the Hanafi school: Imam Abu Hanifa was explicit. If you hold the mushaf, then the salah is batil, null and void.

Now, this became the standard position of the Hanafi school. It is what the Hanafis call the *mufta bihi*, or the fatwa that is given. It is the standard position, and that is why our Hanafi brethren, may Allah bless them and grant them good in this world and the Akhirah, generally speaking, in their subcultures, the concept of carrying a mushaf is alien to them. And if you go to the Shafi'i cultures, the Maliki cultures, the Hanbali cultures, it is very common in the nights of taraweeh to find people carrying the mushaf, no problem.

That having been said, and I'm not going to interfere with the intricacies of the Hanafi madhhab; as I have said, I am more familiar with the Hanbali school, that is the school I typically follow in my personal life. But that having been said, the Hanafis should be aware that the two famous scholars, students of Abu Hanifa, Qadi Abu Yusuf and Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Shaybani (they are called the *sahibayn*, or the *sahiban*, the two main disciples), both of them disagreed with their teacher and mentor Abu Hanifa on this issue, rahimahullahu ta'ala. And they said that if a person were to carry the mushaf, the salah is not batil. But they did say that it is makruh; it should be avoided, but it is not batil.

And later 'ulama extracted reasons for this, and they said that there are two reasons that we can find in the Hanafi school. The first of them: there's too much motion, or harakah, and as you know, during salah you should have a minimal amount of extra motions. And the second, they said, there is an element of imitation, or tashabbuh, of other religious rituals. And fair enough, that's their extrapolation. But others might say that if you're carrying an iPhone and you're just holding it, it's not really... sorry, it's not really too much harakah per se. Or, to get out of the harakah issue, I'm just saying, think about it: if you were to have a mushaf open on a stand, a very large mushaf, and there's a page here and a page here, and you're not touching anything, and you're simply looking at this page and reading, and then you go into ruku', then you stand up, then you look at this page, then you read, then between the taslims, after the taslim, you turn the page... I'm just saying, not trying to cause any issues. But if you want to follow the madhhab, no problem, that's fine; that is the mufta bihi position.

Let me just say that many of my modern Hanafi scholar friends of our times, quite a number of them, I know for a fact that they say to their congregations: look, that's the *mu'tamad*, or the standard position, but especially given our circumstances and whatnot... A number of Hanafi scholars, especially in light of COVID-19 and the lockdown, are saying, you know what, let's follow Imam Abu Yusuf and Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Shaybani's position, that the salah is sahih; it is valid to do that. But in any case, that is your position, what you want to follow. I'm just telling you that this is one position.

The majority of the other scholars have said there is no problem in a normal circumstance. How about now, even more so: you may pick up a mushaf, or in our case an iPhone or whatever it is, just have the app on, and you may read it. It is a nafl salah anyway, and in nafl salah more motions are allowed than in a fard salah anyway. This is the standard. But anyway, if you want to follow a position within your school, then alhamdulillah; I'm not going to ever, ever, ever criticize following a standard madhhab if you stick to that madhhab consistently. **But if you want my humble opinion, then really there is no problem.**

The point of taraweeh is to read long qira'ah of the Qur'an. That's the goal of taraweeh. And that's why Imam Ahmad and others, Imam Malik, explicitly said long qiyams and short sajdahs are better than short qiyams and long sajdahs. For taraweeh, we don't necessarily want to make the sajdahs long; we want to make the reciting long, and we want to read as much Qur'an as possible. How is that going to happen if you're not a hafidh, or even if you are and your hifz is weak and you're not going to be leading? You know, there are very few people whose hifz is that strong that they can read a hizb or a juz'. And that's why we admire and respect our huffadh so much, that they are able to do this. Otherwise, most average huffadh are not able to do that quickly; they're going to take a long time.

And that's why this concession is given, that you may just read from the mushaf. And suppose you are not a hafidh: then in this case you may read what you're familiar with, let's say Juz' 'Amma or Juz' Tabarak or whatever. You may read from that, no problem, inshaAllahu ta'ala.
